purpose_text: On July 19, 2024, the agency issued the RFQ for the placement of an order under the General Services Administration Multiple Award Schedule, Special Item Number 541219 (Budget and Financial Management Services), for internal control support services for the CISA Office of Chief Financial Officer Internal Control Subdivision.
prompt_text: The RFQ, however, further advised vendors that the agency would not issue an award to a vendor “who presents a considerably higher overall price to achieve only slightly better performance capabilities. Consequently, as non-price evaluations become more equal, price may be of greater significance in the trade-off consideration.”
reply_text: The protester also argues that the agency failed to properly consider the qualitative differences between the protester’s and awardee’s past performance records.
reviewer_text: While Guidehouse Inc. does show both strong institutional knowledge of CISA’s Internal Controls program (and is the incumbent, automatically presenting less transition risk) and provided more references of performing similar work as a prime contractor, I do not believe this is worth an extra $3.1 [million].
post_award_status: RFQ 70RCSJ24Q00000072; award to BDO Public Sector, LLC ($10,196,570.06 vs. Guidehouse $13,345,430.25); GAO protest B-423156.2 denied May 22, 2025.
grammar_notes: active_human; firm; concrete; noun_stack; quotes_concrete_detail — CO explicitly credits incumbent/institutional knowledge and quotes concrete ~$3.1M / 23.60% price premium rather than denying without concrete comparison.
plain_speech_gloss: DHS/CISA sought internal control support under GSA SIN 541219; the solicitation warned against paying a steep price for modest extra capability; Guidehouse argued its stronger past performance warranted selection; the contracting officer acknowledged Guidehouse's incumbent and institutional strengths but judged them not worth roughly $3.1 million extra

agency: Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI)
purpose_text: The RFP sought proposals to provide a range of advisory services and support to improve the processes and capabilities surrounding the development, defense, execution, reporting, and process analysis of activities required to develop the NIP submission to the Office of Management and Budget and Congress.
prompt_text: The SOW defined the qualifications for the program manager, including, as relevant here, “Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent PM certification and minimum of seven (7) years relevant experience as a Program Manager within the Federal Government.”
reply_text: In a narrative addressing the required qualifications, according to Guidehouse’s proposal, X “has over 8 years’ experience managing programs with varying degrees of complexity within the Federal Government.”
reviewer_text: Under Section 2 of the proposed candidate’s resume, the Offeror stated in general terms that the candidate has “over eight years of experience managing programs with varying degrees of complexity within the Federal Government.”
post_award_status: Solicitation 2021-20111300002S; award to KPMG LLP ($53,027,362 vs. Guidehouse $29,382,335); GAO protest B-421227.2; B-421227.3 sustained Aug. 26, 2024.
grammar_notes: active_human; nominalized; firm; concrete; noun_stack; penalizes_vagueness — evaluator flags proposal's broad program-management claim as stated in general terms against a seven-year federal PM requirement.
plain_speech_gloss: ODNI sought advisory support for National Intelligence Program budget/process work and required at least seven years of federal program manager experience; Guidehouse's narrative stated the candidate had over eight years managing programs of varying complexity; evaluators cited that wording as stated in general terms
column14: and GAO ultimately sustained the protest on evaluation grounds.

purpose_text: The instant procurement seeks a contractor to provide actionable, timely, relevant, and accurate data-driven analysis and risk reduction guidance to the Insights branch.
prompt_text: The SOW’s vulnerability mitigation planning task required experience performing a “Root Cause and Risk Prioritization Analysis to determine the security posture of stakeholders’ operational cyber security environment” and providing CISA “with tools [] and services to mitigate current and/or future vulnerabilities.”
reply_text: Guidehouse oversaw the development and execution of four [binding operational directives (BODs)] and two Emergency Directives (ED), requiring entities to remediate cyber risks and threats.
reviewer_text: These elements decreased the TET’s confidence level as the quotation lacked specificity to demonstrate the [vendor’s] capability to perform the non-policy compliance work such as performing analysis to determine the security posture of stakeholders’ operational cyber security environment and provide CISA with tools (process focused) and services to mitigate current and/or future vulnerabilities.
post_award_status: RFQ 70RCSJ23Q00000049 (CIO-SP3 task order); award to Accenture Federal Services, LLC ($100,706,093 vs. Guidehouse $100,024,553); GAO protest B-422147; B-422147.2 denied Jan. 25, 2024.
grammar_notes: active_human; nominalized; firm; concrete; noun_stack; penalizes_vagueness — TET faults quotation for lacking specificity on non-policy security-posture analysis and mitigation tools/services despite citing four BODs and two EDs.
plain_speech_gloss: CISA's Insights branch needed data-driven risk-reduction analysis and sought evidence of non-policy vulnerability analysis and mitigation tools/services; Guidehouse highlighted overseeing four BODs and two EDs
column14: but evaluators lowered confidence because the quotation lacked specificity on non-policy compliance work
